items.reason: False positive: neither workflow interpolates event text into a run: step — every untrusted value already arrives via an env: binding, and a blocking, fixture-tested ratchet (scripts/security/check-actions.mjs, run by `npm run security:actions` in ci.yml on every push and PR) enforces that rule tree-wide; I tightened the two jobs' token scopes instead, which is the item's second explore question and was a real over-scope.

lessons: Before treating a D9 'dangerous workflow' finding as real, grep for `${{` INSIDE `run:` block scalars specifically. kp binds every untrusted value (`github.event.issue.body`, `pull_request.head.ref`) into an `env:` block on the same step that carries the `run:` — the correct fix — and scanners that scope their match to the whole step rather than the script text flag exactly those steps. The two files a naive detector names are the two that already got it right.

In this organization's repos, check whether the practice is already enforced by an in-repo ratchet before writing one: kp keeps its gates as dependency-free .mjs under scripts/ with fixtures in scripts/**/__tests__/, wired as a blocking `- run: npm run <gate>` line in ci.yml. check-actions.mjs already implements run-injection, script-injection, untrusted-checkout and no-permissions, and gate-check.test.mjs walks the real tree asserting zero findings. The useful residual work is the question the detector did NOT ask.

When a write-capable job opens its PR or pushes its commit with a PAT (AGENT_PR_TOKEN / AUTOFIX_TOKEN / PIN_PR_TOKEN) rather than GITHUB_TOKEN, the corresponding GITHUB_TOKEN scope is usually dead and can be dropped — the PAT indirection exists so the PR triggers workflows, and shedding the scope is a free least-privilege win on the way. pin-actions.yml was already the correct precedent; agent-dispatch.yml and autofix.yml had drifted from it.
